messages:
alex-finance: FYI - AWS sent a rebill (RB-2024-158) that appears to duplicate credits we already passed to customers via CP-99. Amount is $5,450 positive charge to us. Can partner ops confirm flow?
mira-partner-ops: Which customers/orders are impacted? If we already issued customer credits, we need to decide whether to recover from the partner or absorb.
alex-finance: Invoice attached in billing UI: https://redwood.example.com/billing/INV-AWS-RB-2024-158.pdf. Line note: 'Reseller Rebill - Promo Adjustment' ref aws-ord-9932. No partner id in the line.
jon-ap: AP: hold payment until we have resolution. Need vendor remittance info and supporting docs.
aws-marketplace-bot: Notification: Rebill RB-2024-158 posted 2024-11-20T14:03Z for aws-ord-9932. Amount: 5450.00 USD. Docs: https://console.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/rebills/RB-2024-158 (login required).
mira-partner-ops: I pulled aws-ord-9932 - originally routed via CP-99 (HarborPartners). Harbor sent a ticket saying AWS reprocessed a promo flag and issued a rebill to vendors. They claim they did not request duplicate credits to end customers.
sarah-revops: Revenue question: if we already credited customers, and AWS is now charging us, we likely need to net this against partner commissions or classify as a one-time cost. Need to check contract for clause on partner-induced adjustments.
paul-sales: Harbor is asking us to move quickly; their customer is upset that they saw two credits then a charge. They want us to coordinate communication.
alex-finance: Action items: (1) Mira to ask Harbor for written confirmation of whether they requested the rebill; (2) Jon to keep AP hold; (3) Sarah to draft provisional JE and impact note for November close; (4) Alex to request contract clause re: partner indemnity.
mira-partner-ops: Harbor responded: "We did not request a rebill. We requested a promo rollback in Oct which should have routed a single credit via Harbor. AWS appears to have reprocessed and billed vendors directly." They attached their support thread with AWS.
jon-ap: Keeping hold. Reporting in vendor ledger with note "pending partner substantiation RB-2024-158".
sarah-revops: Draft provisional JE as cost item pending substantiation: DR Partner Dispute Expense 6500 $5,450, CR AWS Payable 2105 $5,450. We'll tag as 'pending partner recovery' in the revenue waterfall.
alex-finance: Contract search: clause 8.3 says partners are liable for misrouted rebates if proven, but requires signed evidence. We'll need Harbor written claim and AWS confirmation.
mira-partner-ops: I opened escalation with AWS PM and Harbor rep included. AWS replied: "RB-2024-158 issued due to duplicate promo flag reconciliation; vendor charges are final unless vendor files dispute within 30 days."
paul-sales: Harbor filed a dispute with AWS and sent us the dispute reference. They asked if we can temporarily credit the customer while AWS resolves.
jon-ap: We should avoid customer credits until we have clear accounting direction. If we credit now and AWS resolves in favor of us, we'll have to re-bill Harbor or the customer.
sarah-revops: I'll prepare two scenarios for close: (A) book as contra-revenue (materiality small) and treat as non-recurring expense; (B) hold as contingent liability if partner dispute likely to succeed. Recommend provisional expense with memo and move to contingent if dispute wins.
alex-finance: Sounds good. Let's reconvene after AWS dispute window or once Harbor provides signed claim. Marking AP hold and provisional JE for Nov. I'll capture in close workbook. :white_check_mark:
